h1: Prince Edward County travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Prince Edward County is a Canada base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Sandbanks Provincial Park, add Picton, and use Wellington to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Prince Edward County International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: Origins
history.text: Settled by indigenous peoples, the county has significant archeological sites.
North Marysburgh, surveyed in 1785 and settled by Loyalist veterans, some of Hessian birth.
The county was created by Upper Canada's founding lieutenant-governor John Graves Simcoe on July 16, 1792.
Hillier, organized in 1823, and named after Major George Hillier, military secretary to Sir Peregrine Maitland.

On January 1, 1998, the Town of Picton, the villages of Bloomfield and Wellington, and the townships of Ameliasburgh, Athol, Hallowell, Hillier, North Marysburgh, Sophiasburgh, and South Marysburgh amalgamated to form a new municipality.
These include the LeVescounte Mounds of the Point Peninsula complex people, built about 2000 years ago.

history.label: Today
history.text: It was named after Prince Edward Augustus, Duke of Kent (the fourth son of King George III and father of Queen Victoria) who was commander-in-chief of British North America.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: Shortly after the American Revolution, the Crown made land grants to some of the earliest United Empire Loyalists to encourage their settlements in Ontario and provide compensation for property lost in the Thirteen Colonies.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The county was originally composed of three townships named in honour of three of George III's daughters.
